text: Hello, everyone. My name is Sara Araújo.
I'm a marine biologist working at the University of Aveiro
in Portugal, and I'll be presenting the Aurora Shiny app, a
tool developed to help standardizing messy biodiversity data sets according
to the Darwin Core.
To start with a small introduction, biodiversity data are often stored
in diverse structures, which makes standardization and
publication through public repositories challenging.
These repositories, such as GBIF and OBIS, require data to be
compliant with the Darwin Core standard.
But the standardization process can sometimes mean
overcoming complex event structures, taxonomic ambiguities, and
geospatial inaccuracies, which can make this whole process
effort, time, and resource-demanding.
Many researchers indicate this step as one of the main
barriers to publishing their data.
And it was with this in mind that we developed an online application
based on R Shiny
that offers a comprehensive and user-friendly workflow for
converting unstructured biodiversity data into
standardized Darwin Core
tables ready for publication.
Through this QR code, you can access
the tool's website. The Aurora Shiny app requires only an
internet connection to work, and the workflow is
structured around eight key steps, which I will be going through
in the next slides.
And to start with the first one, the Aurora Shiny app allows users to
upload their data as a CSV file.
And their tables can then be transformed to a tidy
format if necessary, so one
occurrence per record.
The tables can be uploaded already in a tidy format or transformed

The data set can then be inspected before completing the ingestion, just

suitable Darwin Core term,

ID fields such as Occurrence ID or Events ID,
remarks fields, and dependency fields.

already present in the data set.
The workflow also includes the validation of required terms, and the set
of these required terms can be adjusted
by selecting the target submission repository.
So currently, users can choose between OBIS, GBIF, and
EMODnet Biology as their target submission repository.
The tool also allows the transformation of temporal information
and geographical coordinates to the formats required by Darwin
Core.
